citation.title: Real-Time Control of Advanced Scenarios for Steady-State Tokamak Operation

topic: Lecture review of real-time kinetic/magnetic profile control (SISO and MIMO), burn-control mimicking, and core-edge dual control in DIII-D, JET, JT-60U, Tore Supra and ASDEX Upgrade.
own_question: How can steady-state advanced tokamak scenarios be controlled in real time, and which control issues remain open?
actual_method_and_evidence: Narrative review of prior experiments and modeling, reproducing figures from other papers. It contains no new data and no estimator benchmarking. It mentions JT-60U real-time ion temperature gradient control using fast charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, attributed to cited work. It does not cover KSTAR, BES/ECEI-based estimation of CES reports, or nowcasting.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Reviews describe real-time profile control as depending on real-time measurements of local kinetic parameters, including CXRS-based ion temperature gradient on JT-60U.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a review statement citing Yoshida 2009. It shows that real-time sensing is a control input. It does not show that CES latency limits control or that nowcasting would help.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: No CES report timing, latency or arrival-time information is given.
forbidden_inferences: That CES latency is a demonstrated bottleneck
That our nowcast enables control or deployment
Generalizing to all prior control work
Attributing the JT-60U results to this lecture rather than the cited primary paper
reason_to_include_or_exclude: At most optional generic motivation for real-time profile sensing in control. The primary sources, such as Yoshida 2009, would be better citations; exclusion is preferred.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
